finalText:
Ask: fix the failing test in math.rs - wanted: `cargo test` green.
For you: `math::tests::test_add` now passes. It asserted `add(2, 2) == 5`, which is wrong, so I changed the expected value to 4 in `src/math.rs`. I also removed the "Intentional failing test" comment. `add` itself is correct. `cargo test` now shows 3 passed, 0 failed, and the doc-tests run clean. The LSP daemon isn't installed here, so I couldn't run LSP diagnostics. The cargo build and test run did compile the file.

`Cargo.lock` and `target/` are untracked build output from the test run. I left them and made no commit. I treated this as a tiny fix with no tier-raising facts, so there's no goal object, notepad or reviewer.

toolArgs.name: eval
toolArgs.args: {"language":"js","summary":"Locate math.rs and check the repo layout and git state","code":"const r = await Bun.$`pwd; git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>&1; git status --short 2>&1 | head -20; find . -name math.rs -not -path '*/target/*' 2>/dev/null; find . -name Cargo.toml -not -path '*/target/*' | head`.nothrow().text(); print(r);"}

toolArgs.name: eval
toolArgs.args: {"code":"print(await Bun.$`cat src/math.rs; ls src; cat Cargo.toml; cargo test 2>&1 | tail -40`.nothrow().text());","language":"js","summary":"Read math.rs and run cargo test to see the failure"}

toolArgs.name: edit
toolArgs.args: {"path":"src/math.rs","edits":[{"oldText":"        // Intentional failing test for scenario S2\n        assert_eq!(add(2, 2), 5);","newText":"        assert_eq!(add(2, 2), 4);"}]}

toolArgs.name: eval
toolArgs.args: {"code":"print(await Bun.$`cargo test 2>&1 | tail -15; git status --short`.nothrow().text());","language":"js","summary":"Rerun cargo test to confirm the fix"}
